title.narrative: Sustainable Colombia Facility - IDB Trust Fund

description.narrative:
The Sustainable Colombia Fund is part of the Colombia in Peace strategy for post-conflict and is one of the four trust funds created for the implementation of the Peace Agreement with FARC; specifically with regards to the first component of the Agreement: The Comprehensive Rural Reform.
The main outcome of the Fund is to maximize the environmental, economic, and social dividends of peace in Colombia, primarily in territories at the intersection of armed conflict incidence, strategic areas for sustainable rural development and environmental conservation.
The Fund is initially established for a period of 15 years and will provide medium-term and long-term support to the post-conflict in Colombia.
The specific objectives of the Fund are: (i) to promote conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; (ii) to forge and support sustainable rural development; (iii) to support the implementation of national policies that promote climate change mitigation and reduction of deforestation; (iv) to support capacity building in areas affected by the armed conflict; and (v) to mainstream climate change considerations in the development agenda as a cross-sectoral topic.

Sveriges ambassad har hängivet stöttat Colombias ansträngningar för att uppnå fred i över två årtionden. Som ett resultat av fredsavtalet med FARC, och som svar på de punkter som fastställts genom avtalet, har Colombias regering upprättat en strategi för postkonflikten vid namn Colombia en Paz. Denna strategi består av fyra fonder som etablerats med syfte att dra största möjliga nytta av det internationella utvecklingssamarbetet i landet. Sverige stöder de fyra fonderna. Världsbankens Trust Fond fokuserar på att tillämpa lagen om konfliktens offer (kollektiv gottgörelse) och innefattar ett särskilt avsnitt om tekniskt stöd till ett pilotprojekt inom lantmäteri; FN:s Multi-partner Trust Fund (MPTF) intar ett kortsiktigt perspektiv och åtar strategier för snabba svarsåtgärder; EU:s Trust Fund (EUTF) är en fond med medellångt tidsperspektiv och landsbygdsutveckling som huvudfokus.
Den fjärde fonden, Interamerikanska utvecklingsbankens (IDB) Sustainable Colombia Facility, väntas komplettera de övriga fonderna för postkonflikten genom att främja långsiktiga mål som integrerar social, ekonomisk och miljömässig utveckling i konfliktdrabbade regioner.
Sustainable Colombia Facility söker åtgärda fyra huvudsakliga och sammanlänkade utmaningar: (i) skogsskövling och förlust av naturkapital; (ii) fattigdom på landsbygd och regional utveckling; (iii) bristande institutionell kapacitet och samordning på lokal nivå; och (iv) klimatrelaterade utmaningar. Dessutom väntas initiativet stödja genomförandet av de Globala målen för hållbar utveckling och Colombias nationella bidrag (Intended Nationally Determined Contributions; INDC) till dessa. Fonden prioriterar geografiska områden och provinser som är strategiska för landsbygdsutveckling, miljöskydd och fredsbyggande insatser.

This contribution to a multi-donor funding mechanisms is for a Trust Fund designed to implement Colombia’s Peace Agreement with FARC. The contribution’s objective is to support projects and programmes aimed at maximizing the environmental, economic, and social dividends of peace in Colombia, primarily in territories at the intersection of armed conflict incidence, strategic areas for sustainable rural development and environmental conservation. For this purpose, this facility addresses five objectives: (i) Promoting conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; (ii) Forging and support sustainable rural development; (iii) Supporting the implementation of national policies that promote climate change mitigation and reduction of deforestation; (iv) Supporting capacity building in areas affected by the armed conflict; and (v) Mainstreaming climate change considerations in the development agenda as a cross-sectoral topic.

description.narrative:
The Fund has been progressing in the execution and finalization of various projects included in its portfolio. Following the Norwegian donation made at the end of 2024, the Fund advanced in the structuring of a new projects that aim to support the government of Colombia to implement its Biodiversity Action Plan.
The following are the most relevant achievements during 2025:
Technical Achievements: - The Funds interventions reached 21 departments and 95 municipalities, with a strong focus on national priority areas. Over 64% of municipalities are located in PDET (Territorially Focused Development Programs) subregions, 38% in active deforestation hotspots, and 39% within government-prioritized forest and biodiversity development hubs. - More than 525,000 hectares have been conserved through ecosystem restoration, biodiversity protection, and sustainable forest management, contributing directly to climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts. - The Fund has supported 210,903 hectares under sustainable and low-carbon production models, strengthening 27 agricultural and livestock value chains and promoting climate-resilient rural livelihoods while reducing deforestation and GHG emissions. - Interventions reinforced national and local capacities for deforestation monitoring, land-use planning, and environmental management, enhancing the sustainability and scalability of results. - Fund-supported projects directly benefited 32,616 people, with 46.8% women and strong participation from Afro-Colombian (49.5%) and Indigenous (14.2%) communities, underscoring a commitment to equity, inclusion, and culturally appropriate development.
Capacity Building: During the reporting period, the Fund made substantial progress in strengthening technical and institutional capacities at national, subnational, and community levels, contributing to improved environmental governance, deforestation control, and sustainable rural development.
- Public institutions increasingly rely on data-driven decision-making and coordinated enforcement actions against deforestation. This was possible by enhancing policy design, including green finance and sustainable livestock transformation, and improving data systems, forest monitoring, and early warning mechanisms. - Local governments demonstrate stronger ownership of environmental management and planning by improving forest monitoring, land-use planning, and enforcement capacity while strengthening management of Areas of Special Environmental Interest (AEIA). - Communities are transitioning from extractive to sustainable livelihood models, supported by skills, incentives, and market integration. This is being possible by the delivering of training and technical assistance for sustainable production and climate adaptation and the strengthening of inclusive value chains (cocoa, coffee, forestry, livestock, etc.)
